title: Review: Ideal gas equation and gas laws; Limiting reagent and yield; Atom economy; Brønsted–Lowry acids and bases
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM10#t1 term and clue written for the game; AM10#t2 term and clue written for the game; AM09#t4 term and clue written for the game; AM04#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AB01#N.11, AM04#N.6a, AM09#N.4a, AM10#N.3, AB01#N.4a, AM04#N.15a, AM09#N.6, AM10#N.9, AB01#N.6a, AM04#N.10a, AM09#N.10b, AM10#N.5. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Atom economy
items.clue: Percentage of the total mass of reactants that ends up in the desired product.

items.label: Addition reaction
items.clue: Gives a single product, so 100% of the starting mass ends up in what is wanted.

items.label: Actual yield
items.clue: The mass of product obtained in practice, normally less than the calculated maximum.

items.label: Kelvin
items.clue: Unit of temperature for which gas pressure plots as a straight line through the origin.

questions.stem: Water takes part in two reactions: (1) CH₃NH₂ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃NH₃⁺ + OH⁻ and (2) HBr + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Br⁻. What role does water play?

options.text: A base in (1) and an acid in (2)
An acid in both, as it releases H⁺ in each
Neither: it is neutral, so it is only the solvent
An acid in (1) and a base in (2)

questions.explanation: In (1) water donates H⁺ to the N lone pair of CH₃NH₂ and becomes OH⁻. In (2) it accepts H⁺ from HBr and becomes H₃O⁺. Water is amphiprotic: its role depends on its partner.

questions.stem: A gas syringe contains 2.20 cm³ of an ideal gas at 20 °C and 1.20 × 10⁵ Pa. What amount of gas does it contain? (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
Nitrogen and hydrogen react: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g). A mixture contains 5.60 g of N₂ and 1.50 g of H₂. Which statement is correct? (Aᵣ: H 1.0, N 14.0)

options.text: H₂ is limiting, because a smaller mass of H₂ is present.
H₂ is limiting, because the equation needs three times as much H₂ as N₂.
H₂ is limiting: 0.750 mol H₂ needs 2.25 mol N₂, and only 0.200 mol N₂ is present.
N₂ is limiting: 0.200 mol N₂ needs 0.600 mol H₂, and 0.750 mol H₂ is present.

questions.explanation: n(N₂) = 5.60 ÷ 28.0 = 0.200 mol; n(H₂) = 1.50 ÷ 2.0 = 0.750 mol. N₂ needs 3 × 0.200 = 0.600 mol H₂, which is available, so N₂ runs out first.

questions.stem: Which statement about atom economy and waste in an industrial process is correct?

options.text: The higher the percentage yield, the higher the atom economy, so less waste is produced.
Atom economy counts one molecule of each substance, so the coefficients do not affect it.
A process with an atom economy of 100% produces no waste of any kind at all.
The lower the atom economy, the greater the proportion of reactant mass that becomes waste.

questions.explanation: The mass not in the desired product ends up in by-products, so atom economy and waste are inversely related.

questions.stem: Ammonia reacts with water: NH₃(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq). Which species acts as a Brønsted–Lowry acid in the forward reaction?

options.text: NH₃, as it gains a proton to form NH₄⁺
OH⁻, as it forms when H₂O loses a proton
None, as water is neutral and cannot donate
H₂O, as it donates a proton to NH₃

questions.explanation: In the forward reaction H₂O loses H⁺ (becoming OH⁻) and NH₃ gains it (becoming NH₄⁺). The proton donor, H₂O, is the acid; NH₃ is the base.

questions.stem: A sealed aerosol can is left in a car on a sunny day. At 20 °C the gas inside is at 3.00 × 10⁵ Pa. The can warms to 70 °C; its volume stays constant. What happens to the pressure inside the can?

options.text: It rises to 3.5 times its starting value.
It stays the same, because the volume is fixed.
It rises by about 17%.
It falls by about 15%.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the theoretical yield of a product in a reaction?

options.text: The mass of product actually obtained at the end of the experiment
The total mass of all the reactants put in, since mass is conserved
The mass of product calculated from the amount of the limiting reactant
The mass of product calculated from the reactant with the smaller number of moles

questions.explanation: The theoretical yield is the maximum mass of product, from the limiting reactant and the mole ratio, assuming complete reaction and no losses.

questions.stem: Hydrogen is manufactured by reacting methane with steam: CH₄(g) + H₂O(g) → CO(g) + 3H₂(g). In one batch, 16.0 kg of methane gave 4.80 kg of hydrogen. What is the atom economy for producing hydrogen by this reaction? (Aᵣ: H 1.0, C 12.0, O 16.0)
questions.explanation: 3 × 2.0 ÷ (16.0 + 18.0) × 100 = 6.0 ÷ 34.0 × 100 = 17.6%. The products total is the same: 28.0 + 6.0 = 34.0. The rest of the mass ends up as CO.

questions.stem: Which pair of species is a conjugate acid–base pair?

options.text: H₃PO₄ and HPO₄²⁻
CH₃COOH and NH₃
H₂PO₄⁻ and HPO₄²⁻
HSO₄⁻ and SO₄⁻

questions.explanation: They differ by exactly one proton: H₂PO₄⁻ − H⁺ = HPO₄²⁻. One H fewer and a charge one unit more negative is the signature of a conjugate pair.

questions.stem: A fixed mass of an ideal gas occupies 2.00 × 10⁻³ m³ at 1.00 × 10⁵ Pa and 27 °C. It is compressed to 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m³ and at the same time its temperature rises to 87 °C. What is its new pressure?
questions.explanation: p₂ = 1.00 × 10⁵ × 4.00 × (360/300) = 4.80 × 10⁵ Pa. Compressing and heating both raise the pressure.

questions.stem: Thermite is a mixture of aluminium and iron(III) oxide. 2Al(s) + Fe₂O₃(s) → Al₂O₃(s) + 2Fe(l). A mixture of 10.0 g of Al and 10.0 g of Fe₂O₃ reacts, and 5.60 g of iron is collected. What is the percentage yield of iron? (Molar masses: Al 27.0, Fe₂O₃ 159.6, Fe 55.8 g mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: n(Al) = 0.370 mol; n(Fe₂O₃) = 0.0627 mol. Divided by coefficients, 0.185 against 0.0627: Fe₂O₃ limits. n(Fe) = 2 × 0.0627 = 0.125 mol; theoretical 6.99 g. 5.60 ÷ 6.99 × 100 = 80.1%.

questions.stem: Which reaction has an atom economy of 100% for the product named?

options.text: CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g), making calcium oxide
H₂SO₄(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SO₄(aq) + 2H₂O(l), making sodium sulfate
2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g), making sulfur trioxide
Any reaction that is carried out with a 100% yield

questions.explanation: This reaction has a single product, so every reactant atom ends up in it: 100%.
